# Top 3 changes to `src/billing.ts`

## 1. Break up `generateInvoice` — extract pure helpers (crime_00005)

`generateInvoice` is 204 lines (lines 50–253), 3.4× the 60-line domain threshold. It's the single highest-severity finding in the report (severity 0.9). A function this size almost certainly bundles several responsibilities — tax math, line-item assembly, discount application, totals, persistence — into one body, which is exactly the shape where an agent edits one section without spotting interactions in another.

Extract cohesive sections (tax calc, line-item rendering, totalling) into named, pure helpers and keep `generateInvoice` as a thin orchestrator. This also chips directly at crime_00026 (God File — 310 lines, threshold 300), since `generateInvoice` is most of the file.

## 2. Inject a clock — kill the 7 direct `Date` calls (crime_00019)

Billing is the *worst* place to read the wall clock implicitly: invoice dates, due dates, refund windows, and prorations all depend on "now," but each of the 7 `Date.now()` / `new Date()` calls (lines 57, 63, 92, 198, 238, 250, 273) observes the host clock at runtime. Tests can't pin a fixed moment without monkey-patching, and any temporal logic is impossible to verify deterministically.

Take a `now: () => Date` (or `Clock`) at the module/function boundary and route every timestamp through it. This is a small, mechanical change with an outsized payoff for testability — and it's prerequisite work for trustworthy assertions in `src/billing.test.ts`, which crime_00020 and crime_00037 already flag as weak.

## 3. Disclose the side effects in `calculateRefundPreview` *and* encode the comment rule (crime_00021 + crime_00027)

`calculateRefundPreview` (lines 40–44) has a name that promises a pure preview, but the body calls `saveRefundAudit` and `sendRefundEmail` — an agent treating this as cheap/idempotent could fire real refund emails from a "preview." Either rename to disclose the effect (`processRefundPreview`, `previewAndAuditRefund`) or split the pure calculation from the audit/notify side effects.

While editing this region, lift the prose rule on line 39 — *"Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves"* (crime_00027) — into an actual guard. Right now the policy lives only as a comment, with no nearby code referencing `owner` / `plan` / `billing`. That's a load-bearing invariant hiding from both the type system and the tests. Encode it as a typed predicate (e.g. `assertCanRefund(actor, plan)`) so the rule fails closed instead of relying on a maintainer reading the comment.

---

**Why these three:** they cluster around the highest agent-risk surface in the file. (1) shrinks the per-edit reasoning surface, (2) makes the file testable at all, and (3) closes a quietly dangerous gap where a misleading name and a comment-only rule could let an agent ship a refund bug with full confidence.
